question: What instruments mainly drive the sound?
subtitle: Listen to the dominant sound sources across the track.
hint: Look for synthesizers vs real amplified guitars or wooden acoustic instruments.

options.label: Electronic Synths & Beats
options.description: Produced inside computers with synthesizers, digital drum pads, and samplers

options.label: Amplified Electric Guitars
options.description: Loud electric guitar riffs, chords, solos, or overdriven rock/metal amps

options.label: Natural Acoustic Instruments
options.description: Grand piano, violins, cello, acoustic guitar, brass, or upright bass

options.label: Don't Know / Neither
options.description: A balanced blend of electronic and live instruments, or hard to tell

question: How is the drumbeat or rhythm structured?
subtitle: Listen to the kick drum and overall beat pattern.
hint: Notice whether the drum hits steadily on every beat, skips/rolls, or has a slow bounce.

options.label: Steady Club Thump (1-2-3-4)
options.description: Hypnotic, steady bass drum thumping on every single beat (thump-thump-thump-thump)

options.label: Lively, Skipping or Broken Beats
options.description: Scattered, energetic drum rolls, 2-step shuffle, or funky syncopated groove

options.label: Slow Head-Nod Bounce
options.description: Sluggish half-speed bounce with heavy bass drops (Trap / Dubstep / Hip-Hop)

options.label: Don't Know / Neither
options.description: Standard rock/pop beat, drumless floating music, or hard to tell

question: How does the speed or tempo of the music feel?
subtitle: Focus on the overall speed of the beat or pulse.
hint: Compare it to daily activities like walking, jogging, or sprinting.

options.label: Slow & Leisurely (< 100 BPM)
options.description: Like meditative breathing, a slow dance, or a calm stroll (under 100 BPM)

options.label: Moderate & Steady (100–125 BPM)
options.description: Like an average radio pop song or brisk walking pace (100–125 BPM)

options.label: Fast & Energetic (125+ BPM)
options.description: Brisk workout pace, club dance floor, or all-out sprint (125+ BPM)

options.label: Don't Know / Neither
options.description: Floating without a clear pulse, changing speeds, or hard to tell

question: How intense or rapid is the fast rhythm?
subtitle: Listen to whether the beat is a standard dance pace or an extreme sprint.
hint: Notice if it sprints past 150 BPM, gallops like a motor, or slices drum rolls.

options.label: Blistering Sprint (150+ BPM)
options.description: Frantic, high-velocity speed that feels like a full sprint or high-speed chase

options.label: Relentless Galloping Bassline
options.description: Fast 3-note bass roll humming non-stop behind every beat (Psytrance / Heavy Metal)

options.label: Sliced, Stuttering Drum Breaks
options.description: Rapidly chopped acoustic drum rolls and crashing cymbals (Jungle / Drum & Bass)

options.label: Don't Know / Neither
options.description: Steady club/rock tempo (120–135 BPM) without extreme sprint speed

question: What do the vocals or voices sound like?
subtitle: Focus on how the human voice is delivered.
hint: Notice whether there is singing, rapping/spoken words, or if it is instrumental.

options.label: Purely Instrumental
options.description: No human singing or vocal performances (or only tiny rare snippets)

options.label: Clear Melodic Singing
options.description: Tuneful vocal melodies, pop hooks, or soulful singing

options.label: Rhythmic Rhyming or Spoken Hooks
options.description: Rapped verses, MC chants, or spoken club one-liners over the beat

options.label: Don't Know / Neither
options.description: Other vocal delivery (like harsh screams) or hard to tell

question: How are the vocals processed or performed?
subtitle: Listen to the special character or effect on the voices.
hint: Notice if the voice is screaming, robotic/Auto-Tuned, or soft whispers.

options.label: Aggressive Screams / Growls
options.description: Throat-shredding screams or deep guttural monster growls (Metal / Hardcore)

options.label: Robotic / Auto-Tuned
options.description: Noticeable metallic Auto-Tune pitch snaps or vocoder robot voices

options.label: Soft, Dreamy Whispers
options.description: Intimate airy whispers or ghostly vocals floating deep in echo

options.label: Don't Know / Neither
options.description: Natural human singing/rapping without these extreme effects

question: What emotional mood or atmosphere dominates the music?
subtitle: Focus on the overall feeling the music creates.
hint: Consider whether the vibe is bright and feel-good, dark and sinister, or chaotic rage.

options.label: Sunny, Joyous & Feel-Good
options.description: Bright, celebratory, and optimistic energy that makes you smile

options.label: Dark, Moody & Menacing
options.description: Sinister, creepy, or gloomy vibe like a thriller film or dark warehouse

options.label: Aggressive, Furious & Chaotic
options.description: High-adrenaline rage that makes you want to smash things or mosh

options.label: Don't Know / Neither
options.description: Dreamy, nostalgic, cozy, or neutral club energy

question: Does the track have a nostalgic, cozy, or grand choral feel?
subtitle: Listen to the emotional space and intimacy of the recording.
hint: Notice if it feels like a nostalgic memory, a quiet bedroom, or a grand choir.

options.label: Nostalgic, Dreamy & Bittersweet
options.description: Sentimental longing like an 80s neon sunset, old polaroids, or fond memories

options.label: Quiet, Close-Up & Intimate
options.description: Cozy, personal living-room or bedroom vibe played softly right next to you

options.label: Grand Choir or Group Harmonies
options.description: A large group of voices, church/gospel choir, or operatic chorus singing together

options.label: Don't Know / Neither
options.description: Standard studio/club energy without these specific vibes

question: How does the groove or motion make your body move?
subtitle: Notice the physical sensation of the rhythm.
hint: Notice whether it has a playful bounce, a rigid machine march, or crushing breakdowns.

options.label: Bouncy Swing or Shuffle
options.description: Loose groove with a playful skip that makes you sway or snap your fingers

options.label: Straight Robotic March
options.description: Rigid, mechanical metronome pulse marching strictly on the grid

options.label: Sudden Crushing Breakdowns
options.description: Music abruptly slams to a halt into a slow, crushing head-banging stomp

options.label: Don't Know / Neither
options.description: Standard rhythmic flow, or hard to tell

question: How clean, distorted, or dusty does the audio feel?
subtitle: Listen to the overall studio finish and surface texture.
hint: Notice if it feels sparkling crisp, raw and overdriven, or dusty with vinyl crackle.

options.label: Sparkling Clean & Glossy
options.description: Super crisp, bright modern studio or radio polish with zero grit

options.label: Raw, Gritty & Distorted
options.description: Abrasive crunchy fuzz, roaring overdrive, or blown-out speaker distortion

options.label: Dusty Vinyl Crackle or Retro 8-Bit
options.description: Noticeable record needle crackles, cassette tape hiss, or retro video-game bleeps

options.label: Don't Know / Neither
options.description: Balanced studio sound without extreme gloss, distortion, or crackle

question: Does the bassline have one of these signature styles?
subtitle: Listen closely to how the bass moves and growls.
hint: Notice if the bass slides in pitch, growls like a robot/chainsaw, or slaps funkily.

options.label: Sliding 808 Bass Glides
options.description: Deep bass booms that swoop and slide smoothly up and down in pitch (Trap / Drill / Amapiano)

options.label: Growling Chainsaw / Wobble Bass
options.description: Aggressive metallic robot growls or heavy morphing bass wobbles (Dubstep / Bass House / Neurofunk)

options.label: Funky Thumb-Slap Bass Guitar
options.description: Bouncy electric bass guitar where strings are slapped and popped with a sharp groove

options.label: Don't Know / Neither
options.description: Steady bassline, natural acoustic bass, or none of these special bass styles

question: If synthesizers or studio effects stand out, how do they sound?
subtitle: Listen to the dominant electronic melodies, chords, or space echoes.
hint: Notice whether synths soar like a festival anthem, squelch like acid, or echo in deep space.

options.label: Massive Festival Anthem Chords
options.description: Huge, buzzing walls of synths swelling into an epic hands-in-the-air drop (EDM / Trance)

options.label: Twisting, Rubbery Acid Squelches
options.description: Bubbling, whistling electronic 303 synth lines that warp and squeak (Acid rave sound)

options.label: Cavernous Dub Space Echoes
options.description: Chords or drum hits bouncing repeatedly into deep space with long delay trails

options.label: Don't Know / Neither
options.description: Standard synth melodies, subtle pads, or no synthesizers

question: How does the low end or drum foundation feel?
subtitle: Focus on the weight of the kick drum and bass warmth.
hint: Is it a distorted rave kick, a chest-shaking sub-bass rumble, or warm vintage analog?

options.label: Pounding Distorted Rave Kick
options.description: High-pitched punch followed by an earth-shattering distorted bass roar (Hardstyle / Gabber)

options.label: Chest-Shaking Sub-Bass Rumble
options.description: Ultra-low bass frequencies that physically shake your chest, car, or subwoofer

options.label: Cozy, Warm Analog / Vinyl Tone
options.description: Smooth, rounded 1970s vinyl warmth or mellow Rhodes electric piano glow

options.label: Don't Know / Neither
options.description: Standard punchy drums without extreme sub-bass or distorted rave kicks

question: If guitars are playing, what do they sound like?
subtitle: Focus on the sound and style of the guitars.
hint: Are they bright and chiming, loud and roaring, or gentle nylon acoustic?

options.label: Bright, Chiming Indie Guitars
options.description: Clean or slightly gritty ringing electric guitars that sparkle (Indie / Alternative Rock)

options.label: Roaring Distorted Rock/Metal Riffs
options.description: Loud, heavy electric guitar power chords or screaming solos through an overdriven amp

options.label: Gentle Spanish / Nylon Fingerpicking
options.description: Warm, intimate fingerpicking on a Spanish or classical nylon-string guitar

options.label: Don't Know / Neither
options.description: No guitars in this song, or a different guitar style

question: Do any of these traditional or acoustic instruments stand out?
subtitle: Listen for signature horns, hand percussion, or country twang.
hint: Notice if brass horns, Afro/Latin hand drums, or country steel guitar are prominent.

options.label: Horns & Brass Section
options.description: Trumpets, saxophones, or big band brass blasts (Jazz / Soul / Funk / Salsa)

options.label: Congas, Bongos or Hand Percussion
options.description: Organic hand drums, shakers, or wooden log drums interlocking beneath the beat

options.label: Southern Country Twang
options.description: Weeping pedal steel guitar, banjo, or country fiddle

options.label: Don't Know / Neither
options.description: None of these instruments are present, or hard to tell

question: Does the rhythm match one of these signature regional or freeform styles?
subtitle: Notice if the beat is Latin, Jamaican, Country, or completely drumless.
hint: Think of Reggaeton, island Reggae, Country train beats, or drumless ambient/classical.

options.label: Latin Reggaeton Bounce
options.description: Bouncy Caribbean rhythm ('boom... cha-boom-cha' heard in Reggaeton)

options.label: Relaxed Island / Reggae Off-Beat
options.description: Chords chopping sharply on the off-beats with a laid-back Jamaican sway

options.label: Speeding Country Train Beat
options.description: Fast snare brushes chugging like a steam locomotive (chugga-chugga-chugga)

options.label: Don't Know / Neither
options.description: Standard club/rock/hip-hop beat, or none of these regional rhythms

question: Does the music float freely without a steady beat or drum kit?
subtitle: Listen for whether you can tap your foot to a steady clockwork pulse.
hint: Classical orchestras, solo piano, and ambient soundscapes often breathe freely without drums.

options.label: Drumless & Freely Floating
options.description: Drifting soundscapes or human-led tempo with no steady drum beat to count along with

options.label: Gentle, Cushioned Slow Beat
options.description: Unhurried, soft rhythmic pulse that sways gently without aggressive drums

options.label: Locked, Driving Drum Beat
options.description: Clear, unmistakable drums or electronic beat keeping strict time throughout

options.label: Don't Know / Neither
options.description: Beat comes and goes, or hard to tell
